J. P. Jacobsen, Niels Lyhne, translated by Hanna Astrup Larsen.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/j-p-jacobsen/niels-lyhne/hanna-astrup-larsen

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- J. P. Jacobsen, the author, died 1885.
- Hanna Astrup Larsen, the translator, died 1945.

First publication of the text used: 1919, the English translation (SE colophon: 'Niels Lyhne was published in 1880 by J. P. Jacobsen. It was translated from Danish in 1919 by Hanna Astrup Larsen.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1919, before 1931; a published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after publication, so this work entered it in 2014.
- Country of origin (possible countries: the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa, and Denmark for the original Danish work): the last person to die, Hanna Astrup Larsen, died 1945. With a term of life + 70 years, the text entered the public domain on 1 January 2016 in these countries. Each of the listed countries has a term of life + 70 years or less for these deaths, so the exact country, or a simultaneous first publication in two of them, does not change the result.
- Original work: the Danish original, by J. P. Jacobsen (died 1885), is public domain in Denmark too, where the term is life + 70 years, so it passed on 1 January 1956.

"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States.
